the WARN loop and the check before it run in the same branch (push mode, no preflight refusal). The check before it dies when untrailered(local_main --not main_before) is not empty; a WARN row is untrailered(local_main --not before[i]), the same predicate on the same objects, so every row commit is reachable from main_before and the ancestor check is always true. The only difference: git merge-base itself failing (an object error after rev-list and cat-file read the same objects); not testable without fault injection. Survived the full suite (291/0)

log.showSignature only changes git log, git show and git whatchanged. The census of every git call in the lander (23 subcommands through g(): rev-parse, merge-base, cat-file, rev-list, update-ref, symbolic-ref, status, remote, merge, fetch, diff-tree, config, bundle, write-tree, push, merge-tree, ls-tree, ls-remote, hash-object, diff-index, commit-tree, checkout, add; direct calls: init, interpret-trailers) has no log, show or whatchanged (control needle 'g rev-parse' found, 'g zzneedle' not). The pin is defence in depth; R5-F4 (signature display in the caller config) passes with and without it because every value is read with cat-file. Survived 291/0

ID_RE is ^KEY-(00[1-9]|0[1-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{2,})$ with KEY validated as ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$, matched by bash [[ =~ ]] (POSIX ERE without REG_NEWLINE, LC_ALL=C), so ^ and $ anchor the whole value and a matching value holds only A-Z, 0-9 and '-'; no control character can pass. Measured: without has_ctrl, R5-F13 (CON-9<CR>05 refused) still passes. Survived 291/0

R5-BUNDLE-COPY wants 'bundle sha256 mismatch on the copy'; without the re-hash the changed copy is still refused (rc 1, measured) by a later check (bundle verify, the head ref, or the head type). A changed copy that passed those checks would have to contain the commit --head names, so it delivers the same content-addressed objects (this relies on SHA-1DC collision resistance)
R5-TC: the trailer parser must not read the caller's core.commentChar

defence in depth, one of two layers removed: the merge still passes -s ort, and git merge reads pull.twohead only when no strategy is given; branch.main.mergeOptions is pinned empty separately and the oracle still compares the tree. Measured: R5-N1 (pull.twohead=ours and branch.main.mergeOptions='-s ours' in the caller config) passes. Survived 291/0

defence in depth, the other layer removed: without -s on the command line git merge takes its default strategy from pull.twohead, which is pinned to ort; mergeOptions stays pinned empty and the oracle stays. Measured: R5-N1 passes. Survived 291/0

no git call in the lander passes a pathspec: add -A (no path), checkout -B main <sha>, cat-file blob <sha>, ls-tree <tree>, diff-index/diff-tree/status with no paths (census of the 23 g() subcommands, see F4); --literal-pathspecs only changes how pathspec arguments are read. Survived 291/0
